content: Northwind's checkout service runs on port 8080 with six worker processes.
The media service listens on port 8443 and serves all image traffic over HTTPS.
Image thumbnails at Northwind are generated by the media service, not the API gateway.
Login and token issuance go through the auth service, which listens on port 9001.
Northwind's search service answers queries on port 8983.
Outbound webhooks are dispatched by a dedicated service on port 8081.
The inventory service speaks gRPC on port 8090.
Customer notifications, both push and in-app, come from the notifications service on port 8085.
The payments service accepts mTLS-only connections on port 9443.
Shipping labels are produced by the labels service on port 8082.
Product recommendations are served over gRPC on port 9090.
Fraud screening runs as its own service on port 9002, and checkout consults it before capture.
CSV and PDF exports are handled by the exports service on port 8088.
The pricing service, which owns promotions and discounts, listens on port 8092.
An internal SMTP relay for outbound mail listens on port 2525.
The Northwind API gateway terminates TLS and forwards to internal services.
The Northwind user database is PostgreSQL 16, hosted on the db-main node.
Orders live in their own PostgreSQL 15 instance on db-orders.
The product catalog is stored in MongoDB 7.0 on db-catalog.
Analytics queries run against ClickHouse 24.3 on the olap-1 host.
Northwind's event bus is a three-broker Kafka 3.7 cluster.
The search cluster spans three data nodes, search-1 through search-3.
Northwind switched its session cache from Redis to Memcached in March 2024.
Northwind production runs in the eu-west-1 region, out of Dublin.
Disaster recovery lives in eu-central-1, Frankfurt, as a warm standby.
The production network uses the 10.20.0.0/16 address space.
Production workloads run on a Kubernetes 1.29 cluster with 12 worker nodes.
A keepalived pair of HAProxy boxes sits at the edge in front of the API gateway.
Internal name resolution is CoreDNS, authoritative for the northwind.internal zone.
SSH access to production goes through the jump-1 bastion, and direct logins are refused.
All production hosts sync time from the internal servers ntp-1 and ntp-2.
Production nodes run Ubuntu 22.04 LTS.
Container images are pulled from registry.northwind.internal, never from public registries.
Northwind's staging environment mirrors production but uses a single database replica.
Engineers reach the internal network over WireGuard, since the legacy IPsec VPN is gone.
The API gateway times out upstream calls after 30 seconds.
In February 2024 the anonymous API rate limit was raised to 60 requests per minute.
Authenticated API clients are allowed 600 requests per minute.
Access tokens issued by the auth service expire after 15 minutes.
Refresh tokens stay valid for 60 days.
Product image uploads are capped at 25 MB.
Web sessions expire after 45 minutes of inactivity.
Each checkout instance keeps a pool of 20 Postgres connections.
Search queries are killed if they run past 800 ms.
Failed webhook deliveries are retried five times with exponential backoff.
List endpoints cap the page size at 200 items.
Passwords must be at least 12 characters long, and rotation is not forced.
The payments client trips its circuit breaker after five consecutive failures.
Internal service certificates come from the in-house CA and are rotated every 90 days automatically.
Search cluster escalations page Priya Nair first.
Marcus Webb's team owns the payments service.
Checkout belongs to the Storefront team, led by Elena Petrova.
The platform team under Tomasz Kowalski runs the Kubernetes cluster.
Ines Fuentes is the DBA responsible for db-main and db-orders.
Aiko Tanaka leads security, and new external integrations need her team's review.
Dmitri Volkov owns the media pipeline end to end.
Northwind's on-call rotation hands off every Monday at 09:00 local time.
If the primary on-call has not acknowledged a page within 15 minutes, the secondary is paged.
Sam Okafor's data engineering group owns ClickHouse and the olap-1 host.
Rafael Ortiz coordinates the incident-commander rotation.
INC-2405: on 14 May 2024 an unbounded facet query OOM-killed two search data nodes, and results were degraded for 35 minutes.
INC-2401: Kafka partition leaders flapped for an hour on 22 January 2024 after faulty NIC firmware on broker-2.
INC-2311: on 8 November 2023 payment-provider timeouts cascaded into checkout, and this incident is why the circuit breaker exists.
INC-2407: a webhook retry storm on 2 July 2024 hammered a partner endpoint, and a retry cap was added afterwards.
INC-2402: billing reconciliation skipped invoices dated 29 February 2024 because of a leap-day parsing bug.
INC-2404: a bad CoreDNS push on 18 April 2024 broke internal service discovery for 25 minutes.
INC-2406: thumbnails lagged six hours on 11 June 2024 after a misconfigured media queue consumer.
INC-2312: db-main failed over to its replica on 19 December 2023 after a disk started throwing errors, and writes failed for roughly four minutes.
INC-2408: on 5 August 2024 a rate-limiter misconfiguration throttled logged-in users at the anonymous limit.
INC-2409: an expired internal certificate on the inventory service dropped gRPC calls on 17 September 2024 until renewal automation was fixed.
Northwind moved search off Elasticsearch and onto OpenSearch in September 2023. The cluster now runs OpenSearch 2.13.
In June 2024 Northwind moved media and artifact storage to a MinIO cluster spanning stor-1 through stor-4.
Northwind retired Jenkins in January 2024, and all pipelines now run on GitLab CI.
Monitoring moved from Nagios to Prometheus and Grafana in mid-2023.
The orders database was upgraded from PostgreSQL 13 to 15 in February 2024.
Checkout was carved out of the old PHP monolith back in 2022.
Services moved from VM deployments onto Kubernetes in November 2023.
Billing went event-driven in October 2024, and invoices are now built from Kafka events.
The API gateway was swapped from Nginx to Envoy in April 2023.
TLS 1.0 and 1.1 were disabled at the edge in 2023, and the minimum is now TLS 1.2.
db-main takes a full backup nightly at 01:00 UTC.
WAL segments are shipped to object storage every five minutes.
Database backups are kept for 30 days, then deleted.
Once a quarter, a production backup is restored into staging to prove the backups are real.
Application logs are retained for 90 days.
Audit logs are kept for 400 days to satisfy compliance.
PII from deleted accounts is purged within 14 days.
The disaster recovery plan targets an RPO of 10 minutes and an RTO of four hours.
An external firm runs a penetration test every October.
Backend Python services run on Python 3.12.
The inventory and recommendations services are written in Go 1.22.
The storefront frontend builds on Node 20 LTS.
Terraform is pinned at 1.7 across all environments.
All containers build from a minimal Ubuntu 22.04 base image pinned by digest.
Release trains leave every Tuesday and Thursday.
Python services talk to Postgres through psycopg 3.
The public API sits at version v2, and v1 sunsets in December 2026.
The new-checkout-flow flag is at 25% of traffic.
guest-checkout went to 100% in May 2024, and the flag is due for cleanup.
The ai-recommendations flag is enabled for staff accounts only.
The legacy-wishlist flag is switched off and its code is scheduled for removal.
express-shipping is enabled only for EU customers.
fraud-model-v2 runs in shadow mode, with scores logged but not enforced.
Feature flags come from an in-house flag service, and clients cache flag state for 60 seconds.
dark-mode shipped to everyone in 2023 and is no longer gated.
Checkout calls the payments and inventory services synchronously. Everything else is async.
Checkout's availability SLO is 99.95% monthly.
Search commits to a p99 latency of 300 ms.
The API gateway carries an availability SLO of 99.9%.
When a service burns its monthly error budget, its deploys freeze until the budget recovers.
Card processing is handled by an outside provider, Paylode.
Parcelio prints Northwind's shipping labels and allows 5 requests per second.
Transactional email goes out via Mailhawk, with a quota of 100,000 messages a day.
The webhook SLO is 99% of deliveries within 60 seconds.
Exports are limited to three concurrent jobs per tenant.
Northwind's nightly batch job starts at 02:00 UTC and runs for about 40 minutes.
The search service rebuilds its full index from the catalog every Sunday night.
Northwind's billing service reconciles invoices once per day at 13:00 UTC.
Deploys are Git-driven, applied by the release pipeline. The merged state of main is what runs.
Until March 2024, Northwind cached user sessions in Redis.
Until September 2023, Northwind's search ran on Elasticsearch 7.
Until June 2024, media assets and build artifacts lived on an NFS filer named files-01.
Until January 2024, Northwind's builds ran on a Jenkins server named build-01.
Until February 2024, anonymous API traffic was capped at 30 requests per minute.
Nagios handled Northwind's host and service checks until mid-2023.
